any person, or any class of persons, authorised for the purposes of this section by the regulations.
The Registrar must establish and keep a Register of land claims.
The Register of Aboriginal Land Claims is to be kept in a form prescribed by the regulations or, if no form is prescribed, in a form determined by the Registrar.

heading.b: Contents of Register of Aboriginal Land Claims

block.txt: The Register of Aboriginal Land Claims is to include the following information—
a number for each individual land claim (sequential over time),
the name of the Aboriginal Land Council that made the land claim,
a description of the land claimed,
the parish or parishes and the county or counties that the land claimed is within,
the local government area or areas that the land claimed is within,
the date of lodgment with the Registrar of the land claim,
the date of determination of the land claim by the Crown Lands Minister (within the meaning of section 36),
such other information prescribed by the regulations.

heading.b: Registrar may request information from Crown Lands Minister

block.txt: The Registrar may request the Crown Lands Minister (within the meaning of section 36) to provide information relating to a land claim that is listed on the Register of Aboriginal Land Claims.

heading.b: Regulations may provide for public inspection of Register

block.txt: The regulations may make provision for public inspection of the Register of Aboriginal Land Claims.
(cf former section 49B)
The Registrar must establish and keep a Register of Aboriginal Owners.
The Register is to be kept in a form prescribed by the regulations or, if no form is prescribed, in a form determined by the Registrar.

heading.b: Contents of Register of Aboriginal Owners

block.txt: (cf former section 49C)
The Registrar is to enter in the Register of Aboriginal Owners—
the names of Aboriginal persons who have a cultural association with land in the State, and
the location of the land with which the Aboriginal person has a cultural association, and
the nature of the cultural association that the Aboriginal person has with the land.
The name of an Aboriginal person must not be entered in the Register unless the Aboriginal person—
is directly descended from the original Aboriginal inhabitants of the cultural area in which the land is situated, and

has a cultural association with the land that derives from the traditions, observances, customs, beliefs or history of the original Aboriginal inhabitants of the cultural area in which the land is situated, and
has consented to the entry of the person’s name in the Register.
The Registrar is to give priority to the entry in the Register of the names of Aboriginal persons who have a cultural association with—
lands listed in Schedule 14 to the NPW Act, and
lands to which section 36A applies.
Schedule 14 to the NPW Act lists lands of cultural significance to Aboriginal persons that are reserved or dedicated under that Act.

Section 36A applies to lands that are the subject of a claim by one or more Aboriginal Land Councils under section 36 of this Act and that the Crown Lands Minister is satisfied would be claimable lands except for the fact that the lands are needed, or likely to be needed, for the essential public purpose of nature conservation.

heading.b: Requests for entry of names in Register

block.txt: (cf former section 49D)
Any Aboriginal person may make a written request to the Registrar to enter the name of an Aboriginal person in the Register of Aboriginal Owners.
A request must specify the land with which the Aboriginal person nominated for inclusion in the Register has a cultural association and the cultural area in which the land is situated.
A request must not be made without the written consent of the Aboriginal person nominated for inclusion in the Register.

heading.b: Requests for opening of parts of Register of Aboriginal Owners

block.txt: (cf former section 49E)

The Minister administering the NPW Act may request the Registrar to open a part of the Register of Aboriginal Owners for the purpose of entering the names of Aboriginal persons who have a cultural association with lands that the Minister administering the NPW Act has recommended to the Governor be listed in Schedule 14 to that Act.
The Registrar is to comply with a request made by a Minister under this section.

An Aboriginal person or an Aboriginal Land Council may also request the Registrar to open a part of the Register for the purpose of entering the names of Aboriginal persons who have a cultural association with a particular area of land specified in the request.
(cf former section 49F)
The Registrar may amend information on, remove information from or otherwise rectify the Register of Aboriginal Owners in accordance with this section.
The Registrar may amend information on, or remove information from, the Register of Aboriginal Owners if the Registrar considers the information is false, erroneous or misleading.
Before amending or removing information relating to an Aboriginal person under subsection (1A), the Registrar must give the Aboriginal person—
written notice of the proposed change, and
an opportunity to make submissions in relation to the proposed change.
The Registrar may rectify the Register of Aboriginal Owners at the request of an Aboriginal person who—
considers the Aboriginal person’s name has been wrongly entered on or omitted from the Register, or
considers an amendment made by the Registrar under subsection (1A) is incorrect.

An Aboriginal person who has made a request under subsection (1C) may appeal to the Court if the Registrar fails or refuses to rectify the Register in the manner requested within 6 months after the making of the request.
On the hearing of an appeal under this section, the Court may—
order the Registrar to rectify the Register, or
decline to order that the Register be rectified, or
make such other order as to the Court appears appropriate.
An appeal is to be made within the time and in the manner provided by the rules of the Court.
The Registrar has the right to appear and be heard by the Court in the appeal proceedings.
In deciding an appeal, the Court—
has the functions and discretions of the Registrar under this Part, and
is not bound by the rules of evidence and may inform itself on any matter in any way that the Court considers to be just.
A decision of the Court on an appeal is final and is to be given effect to as if it were the decision of the Registrar.
The Court may award costs in an appeal under this section in exceptional circumstances only.

heading.b: Reference by Registrar to Land and Environment Court

block.txt: (cf former section 49G)
The Registrar may refer to the Court, for decision by the Court—
a request for the entry of the name of an Aboriginal person in the Register of Aboriginal Owners, or
a request for the omission of the name of an Aboriginal person from the Register, or
any other question arising under this Part in relation to the keeping of the Register by the Registrar.
The Chief Judge of the Court is to determine whether or not the Court should deal with the request or question.
The Court may—
hear and determine the request or question, or
refer the request or question back to the Registrar, with such directions or recommendations as the Court considers appropriate.
The Court may hear and determine a part of a question and refer the remainder back to the Registrar.
The Registrar is to give effect to a determination of the Court under this section.

block.txt: Every Local Aboriginal Land Council must prepare—
a code of conduct to be observed by all officers and members of staff of the Council, and
a code of conduct to be observed by all members of the Council.
The New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council must prepare a code of conduct to be observed by all councillors and members of staff of the Council.
A code of conduct prepared under this section must be submitted to the Registrar for approval.
The code must be prepared and submitted within the time directed by the Registrar.
A code of conduct prepared under section 177 may declare a specified provision of the code to be a dismissal provision for this Division.
The Registrar may prepare and issue a model code of conduct.
A Council may, but need not, adopt the model code.
The regulations must prescribe a code of conduct for Aboriginal Land Councils (the prescribed code of conduct).
The prescribed code of conduct is the code of conduct for an Aboriginal Land Council until a code of conduct is approved for the Aboriginal Land Council under this Division.
An Aboriginal Land Council may, with the approval of the Registrar, amend or replace a code of conduct.

An Aboriginal Land Council may, by resolution at a meeting, remove an officer from office if the Council is satisfied that the officer has breached a dismissal provision of the code of conduct for the Council.
The Aboriginal Land Council must not remove an officer from office under this section unless the Council has—
at least 14 days before the meeting, given the officer notice of the Council’s intention to consider the alleged breach, and
given the officer an opportunity to make submissions about the alleged breach.
A notice of intention to consider an alleged breach must specify—
the date of the meeting at which the matter is to be considered, and
particulars of the alleged breach.
This section does not affect other action that may be taken under this Part in relation to an alleged breach of a dismissal provision.

heading.b: Duties of officers and staff of Aboriginal Land Councils

block.txt: A person who is an officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council or an advisory committee must—
act honestly, in good faith and in the best interests of the Aboriginal Land Council, and
exercise a reasonable degree of care and diligence in carrying out the person’s functions under this or another Act, and
act for a proper purpose in carrying out the person’s functions under this or another Act, and
not use the person’s position for personal advantage.
This section does not give rise to, and cannot be taken into account in, a civil cause of action.

block.txt: For the purposes of this Subdivision, a pecuniary interest is an interest a person has in a matter because of a reasonable likelihood or expectation of appreciable financial gain or loss to the person or another person with whom the person is associated as provided by this section.

A person does not have a pecuniary interest in a matter if the interest is so remote or insignificant that it could not reasonably be regarded as likely to influence any decision the person might make in relation to the matter.
A person has a pecuniary interest in a matter if the pecuniary interest is the interest of—
the person, or
another person with whom the person is associated as provided by this section.
A person is taken to have a pecuniary interest in a matter if—
the person’s spouse or de facto partner, a relative of the person or a partner or employer of the person has a pecuniary interest in the matter, or
the person, or a nominee, partner or employer of the person, is a member of a company or other body that has a pecuniary interest in the matter.
De facto partner is defined in the Interpretation Act 1987, section 21C.
However, a person is not taken to have a pecuniary interest in a matter as referred to in subsection (4)—
if the person is unaware of the relevant pecuniary interest of the spouse, de facto partner, relative, partner, employer or company or other body, or
just because the person is a member of, or is employed by, a local council or a statutory body or is employed by the Crown, or

just because the person is a member of, or a delegate of a council to, a company or other body that has a pecuniary interest in the matter, so long as the person has no beneficial interest in any shares of the company or body.

heading.b: Duty of officers and staff to disclose pecuniary interests

block.txt: A person who is an officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council must disclose the nature of a pecuniary interest in a matter if—
the Council is considering or discussing the matter, and
the person is present at a meeting of the Council, or the Board of the Council, at which the matter is being considered or discussed.
The person must make the disclosure to the meeting as soon as practicable.
The disclosure must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.
Unless the Aboriginal Land Council decides otherwise, the person must not be present at, or in sight of, the meeting of the Aboriginal Land Council—
when the matter is being considered or discussed by the Council, or
when the Council is voting on a question in relation to the matter.

A person does not breach this section if the person did not know and could not reasonably be expected to have known that the matter considered or discussed was a matter in which the person had a pecuniary interest.
An officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council may give a written notice (a general disclosure notice)—
to a meeting of the Aboriginal Land Council, and
to the effect that the officer or member of staff, or the officer’s or staff member’s spouse, de facto partner or relative, is—
a member or employee of a specified company or other body, or
a partner or employee of a specified person.
A general disclosure notice given and not withdrawn is sufficient disclosure of the matters disclosed in the notice for the purposes of future meetings of the Aboriginal Land Council.

heading.b: Duty of consultants to disclose pecuniary interests

block.txt: A consultant who is engaged by an Aboriginal Land Council and who gives advice on a matter at a meeting of the Council must disclose the nature of each pecuniary interest the person has in the matter to the meeting at the time the advice is given.
The person is not required to disclose the person’s interest as a consultant.

A person does not breach this section if the person did not know and could not reasonably be expected to have known that the matter on which the advice was given was a matter in which the person had a pecuniary interest.

disciplinary action—see section 196.
member of staff means—

officer of an Aboriginal Land Council includes a former officer of the Aboriginal Land Council.
An Aboriginal Land Council or a Board of a Local Aboriginal Land Council may, by resolution at a meeting, formally censure an officer or member of staff of the Council for misconduct.
A formal censure resolution may be passed only if the Council or Board is satisfied that the officer or member of staff has engaged in misconduct on one or more occasions.
The procedure for consideration of a formal censure motion is as follows—
notice of the motion must be included in the notice given for the next meeting of the Council,
the notice of the motion must specify the grounds on which the Council or Board is satisfied that the officer or member of staff should be censured,
the officer or member of staff to whom the motion relates must be—
notified of the motion, and
allowed to—
address the meeting, or
give a written explanation that must be read to the meeting,
voting on the question of the formal censure must be by secret ballot.

The Council or Board is taken to have formally censured the officer or member of staff if at least a majority of the members of the Council or Board attending the meeting vote in favour of the formal censure of the officer or member of staff.
A person may make a complaint to the Registrar that an officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council has engaged in misconduct.
A complaint need not be in writing.
The Registrar may request a person who makes a complaint to provide, within a specified period, further information in relation to a matter arising from the complaint.

block.txt: The Registrar may conduct an investigation for the purpose of deciding whether an officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council has engaged in misconduct and should be subject to disciplinary action.
The Registrar may conduct the investigation—
on the Registrar’s own initiative, or
on the basis of a complaint made to the Registrar that the officer or member of staff has engaged in misconduct, or
on the basis of a report by the Independent Commission Against Corruption, or
on the basis of a report by the Ombudsman.
The Registrar may request the Aboriginal Land Council to provide the Registrar with a report in relation to the alleged misconduct of the officer or member of staff.
This section authorises the Independent Commission Against Corruption or the Ombudsman to make a report to the Registrar for the purposes of this section or another provision of this Act.
The Registrar may decide not to conduct an investigation in relation to a complaint, including if satisfied of the following—
the alleged misconduct is trivial or does not warrant investigation or further investigation,
the alleged misconduct has been investigated by another authority or is the subject of other proceedings under this or another Act,
the alleged misconduct should be referred to another authority for investigation or it is not appropriate that the Registrar investigate the alleged misconduct,
the alleged misconduct should not be the subject of disciplinary action under this Division or that no further action is warranted,
the alleged misconduct occurred more than 2 years before the complaint or allegation was made and the Registrar is not satisfied as to the reasons for the delay in making the complaint or allegation,
there are insufficient particulars provided in relation to the alleged misconduct to allow the Registrar to investigate the alleged misconduct,
the complaint was not made in good faith,
the person making the complaint has not responded to a request by the Registrar for further information within the time specified by the Registrar.
If the Registrar decides not to conduct an investigation in relation to a complaint, the Registrar must give written notice of the decision to the person who made the complaint.

The Registrar must give written notice to an officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council if the Registrar decides to conduct an investigation in relation to the alleged misconduct of the officer or member of staff.
The notice must—
notify the person about the decision to conduct the investigation, and
describe the nature of the complaint or allegation under investigation.
The Registrar may decide to terminate an investigation and take no further action in relation to the alleged misconduct to which the investigation relates.
The Registrar must give written notice of the decision to—
each person who made a written complaint about the alleged misconduct, and
the officer or member of staff to whom the investigation relates.
This section applies if the Registrar decides to conduct an investigation in relation to an officer of an Aboriginal Land Council.

The Registrar may, by written notice, suspend the officer from holding office if the Registrar is satisfied the alleged misconduct is so serious as to threaten the proper operation of the Aboriginal Land Council.
The suspension has effect until whichever of the following occurs first—
the end of the period of 6 months after the date of the notice of suspension,
the Registrar decides not to take disciplinary action against the officer,
the Registrar decides to take disciplinary action against the officer.
Subsection (3) does not apply if the Registrar refers the alleged misconduct to the Tribunal under Subdivision 4.

block.txt: The Registrar may take action under this Subdivision (disciplinary action) against an officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council if the Registrar is satisfied that—
the officer or member of staff has engaged in misconduct, and
the disciplinary action is warranted.
The Registrar must give written notice to the officer or member of staff of a decision of the Registrar to take disciplinary action, including a statement of reasons for the decision.
The Registrar may take one or more of the following actions against an officer of an Aboriginal Land Council—
counsel or reprimand the officer,
direct the officer to cease engaging in the misconduct,
direct the officer to apologise for the misconduct in the way required by the Registrar,
direct the officer to undertake training,
direct the officer to participate in mediation,
suspend the officer from office,
remove the officer from office or recommend that the Aboriginal Land Council remove the officer from office,
disqualify the officer from holding office in an Aboriginal Land Council for a period of not more than 2 years,
recommend that the Aboriginal Land Council take other action against the officer.
If the Registrar decides to suspend an officer under subsection (1)(f), the Registrar must give the officer written notice of—
the period of suspension, which must not be more than 2 years, and
the date on which the suspension commences, which must be at least 7 days after the date the notice is given to the officer.
The Registrar must not remove an officer from office under subsection (1)(g) or (h) unless the Registrar has—
given the officer written notice of the intention to remove the officer from office, and
considered submissions made by the officer within 14 days after receiving the notice, and
consulted with the Aboriginal Land Council.

heading.b: Disciplinary action against member of staff

block.txt: The Registrar may take one or more of the following actions against a member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council—
counsel or reprimand the member of staff,
disqualify the member of staff from holding office in an Aboriginal Land Council for a period of not more than 2 years,
recommend that the Aboriginal Land Council dismiss the member of staff,
recommend that the Aboriginal Land Council take other action against the member of staff,
if the member of staff is the chief executive officer of a Local Aboriginal Land Council or the Chief Executive Officer of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council—
direct the member of staff to undertake training, or
direct the member of staff to participate in mediation.

heading.b: Appeals against disciplinary action by Registrar

block.txt: An officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council may appeal to the Tribunal against a decision of the Registrar to take disciplinary action against the officer or member of staff.
An appeal under this section is an external appeal to the Tribunal for the purposes of the Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 2013.

For the purposes of subsection (1), a decision to take disciplinary action includes a decision to suspend an officer of an Aboriginal Land Council from holding office during the investigation of alleged misconduct.
An appeal may not be made more than 28 days after the date notice of the decision was given to the officer or member of staff.
The Tribunal may stay the decision until the Tribunal determines the appeal.
The Tribunal may—
confirm the decision, or
quash the decision, or
amend the decision consistently with the powers of the Registrar.
If the decision is amended, the amended decision has effect as if it had been made by the Registrar.
If a decision to suspend an officer is quashed, any fee or other remuneration withheld during the period of suspension is payable to the officer.

block.txt: The Registrar may refer the alleged misconduct of an officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council for the consideration of the Tribunal instead of taking disciplinary action.
The Registrar must give written notice of the referral to the officer or member of staff.
The referral must occur by a report (the referral report)—
presented to the Tribunal by the Registrar, and
containing or accompanied by material and observations the Registrar considers appropriate.
The Registrar may, by written notice, suspend an officer of an Aboriginal Land Council from holding office if—
the Registrar decides to refer alleged misconduct of the officer to the Tribunal under this Subdivision, and
the Registrar is satisfied the alleged misconduct is so serious as to threaten the proper operation of the Council.
The suspension continues until the Tribunal—
determines the matter, or
decides not to conduct proceedings into the matter, or
revokes the suspension under subsection (3).
The Tribunal may, if it considers it appropriate, revoke the suspension of an officer under this Division.

officer and member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council have the same meanings as in Division 4.
referral report, for a referred matter, means the report of the Registrar under section 200 that referred the matter to the Tribunal.
referred matter means a matter referred to the Tribunal under Subdivision 4.

heading.b: Tribunal to decide whether or not to conduct proceedings

block.txt: The Tribunal must decide whether or not to conduct proceedings into a referred matter having considered—
the referral report for the matter, and
other matter the Tribunal considers relevant.
If the Tribunal decides not to conduct proceedings into a referred matter, it must provide a written statement of its decision, and the reasons for its decision, to—
the officer or member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council to whom the referral report relates, and
the Aboriginal Land Council or Board of the Aboriginal Land Council, and
the Registrar.
The Registrar must be a party to proceedings conducted by the Tribunal into a referred matter.

heading.b: Circumstances in which Tribunal may dispense with hearing

block.txt: The Tribunal may determine a referred matter without a hearing if—
the Tribunal has considered—
the referral report for the matter, and
other matter the Tribunal considers relevant, and
the Registrar and the person to whom the referral report relates have agreed that the proceedings may be determined without a hearing, and
there are no material facts in dispute between the Registrar and the person, and
in the opinion of the Tribunal, public interest considerations do not require a hearing.
The Tribunal may suspend an officer of an Aboriginal Land Council from holding office pending the determination of a referred matter if—
the referred matter relates to the alleged misconduct of the officer, and
the alleged misconduct is so serious as to threaten the proper operation of the Council, and
there appears to be sufficient evidence to support the allegation.
The Tribunal may do one or more of the following if it finds that the conduct of an officer of an Aboriginal Land Council to which a referred matter relates warrants action under this section—
counsel or reprimand the officer,
direct the officer to cease engaging in the misconduct,
direct the officer to apologise for the misconduct in the way required by the Tribunal,
direct the officer to undertake training,
direct the officer to participate in mediation,
suspend the officer from office,
disqualify the officer from holding office in an Aboriginal Land Council for a period of not more than 5 years,
order the officer to pay a pecuniary penalty of up to $11,000,
order the officer to reimburse the Aboriginal Land Council for any loss incurred by the Council,
remove the officer from office or recommend that the Aboriginal Land Council remove the officer from office,
recommend that the Aboriginal Land Council take other action against the officer.
The Tribunal may do one or more of the following if it finds that the conduct of a member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council to which a referred matter relates warrants action under this section—
counsel or reprimand the member of staff,
recommend that the Council take specified disciplinary action against the member of staff, including counselling or reprimanding the member of staff,
disqualify the member of staff from holding office in an Aboriginal Land Council for a period of not more than 5 years,
recommend that the Aboriginal Land Council dismiss the member of staff,
recommend that the Aboriginal Land Council take other action against the member of staff,
if the member of staff is the chief executive officer of a Local Aboriginal Land Council or the Chief Executive Officer of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council—
direct the member of staff to undertake training, or
direct the member of staff to participate in mediation.
The Tribunal may deal with one or more complaints or allegations about a person in the same proceedings.
The Tribunal may deal with conduct of a person as if a complaint or allegation (the additional complaint or allegation) had been made about the conduct and referred to the Tribunal if—
the Tribunal is conducting proceedings under this Part in relation to a complaint or allegation against the person (the original complaint or allegation), and
information about the conduct has arisen in the proceedings, and
in the opinion of the Tribunal, a complaint or allegation could have been made against the person about the conduct.
The Tribunal may deal with the additional complaint or allegation—
whether or not the additional complaint or allegation could have been made against the person instead of or in addition to the original complaint or allegation, and
whether or not the additional complaint or allegation could have been made by the person who made the original complaint or allegation.
The Tribunal may deal with an additional complaint or allegation after an adjournment, if any, the Tribunal considers just and equitable in the circumstances.
The Tribunal may do one or more of the following in relation to an additional complaint or allegation—
reconsider a decision under section 205 to determine proceedings on the original complaint or allegation without a hearing,
recommence proceedings by way of hearing for—
the original complaint or allegation, or
the original complaint or allegation and the additional complaint or allegation,
decide, in accordance with section 205, to determine proceedings without a hearing in relation to either or both of the following—
the original complaint or allegation,
the additional complaint or allegation.
The Tribunal may refer a matter before it under this Act to an authority if—
the Tribunal considers that it is more appropriate that the authority deal with the matter, and
the authority agrees to the referral.

heading.b: Investigation and administration of Aboriginal Land Councils
Appointment of investigator into Aboriginal Land Councils

block.txt: (cf former section 56D(1)–(4))

The Minister may appoint an investigator, from a list of investigators jointly prepared by the Chief Executive and the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, to investigate the affairs, or specified affairs, of an Aboriginal Land Council, including its efficiency and effectiveness.

The Minister may appoint an investigator to investigate the affairs of a Local Aboriginal Land Council only with the approval of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council or on the recommendation of the Registrar with the approval of that Council.
The Minister must prepare a report in writing of the Minister’s reasons for appointing an investigator to investigate the efficiency and effectiveness of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.
The Minister is to cause a copy of such a report to be laid before both Houses of Parliament as soon as practicable after the investigator is appointed.

The investigator is to be paid out of the funds of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council. However, in the case of an investigator appointed to investigate the affairs, or specified affairs, of a Local Aboriginal Land Council, the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may recover that amount from the Council concerned.

heading.b: Contents of investigator’s instrument of appointment

block.txt: The instrument by which the Minister appoints an investigator under this Division must specify the following—
whether all or only specified affairs of the Aboriginal Land Council concerned are to be investigated,
the time within which the report required to be prepared by the investigator under section 219 is to be delivered to the Minister, or the Minister and the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council,
the term of office of the investigator,
the functions and duties of the investigator,
unless remuneration for investigators appointed under this Division is prescribed by the regulations—the remuneration of the investigator,
any other matter prescribed by the regulations.

The instrument may also contain provision for the payment to the investigator of remuneration in addition to the remuneration specified in the instrument. For example, the instrument could provide for the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council to approve the payment of additional remuneration that it is satisfied is reasonable.

heading.b: Aboriginal Land Councils to assist investigators

block.txt: (cf former section 56D(5)–(7))

The Chairperson of an Aboriginal Land Council and any other person who has possession or control of any records of the Council must, if required to do so by an investigator who produces evidence of his or her appointment, provide the investigator with—
access to such of the records as relate to the affairs being investigated, and
information that the Chairperson or other person is able to give in relation to those records and affairs, and
authorities or orders on bankers and others that relate to those records or affairs and that the Chairperson or other person is able to provide.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of an individual—30 penalty units, or
in the case of a corporation—60 penalty units.
If a record—
is not in writing, or
is not written in the English language, or
is not decipherable on sight,

a requirement to provide access to the record is not complied with unless access is provided to a statement, written in the English language and decipherable on sight, that contains all the information in the record.
A person must not hinder, obstruct or delay an investigator in the exercise of his or her functions.
Maximum penalty—60 penalty units.
(cf former section 56D(8))
The investigator is to report on the investigation—
in the case of an investigation of the affairs of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council—to the Minister,
in any other case—to the Minister and the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.

heading.b: Minister may extend term of office of investigator

block.txt: The Minister may extend the term of office of an investigator appointed under this Division to investigate the affairs, or specified affairs, of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.

The Minister may, with the consent of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, extend the term of office of an investigator appointed under this Division to investigate the affairs, or specified affairs, of a Local Aboriginal Land Council.
The Minister may, at any time, remove an investigator appointed under this Division to investigate the affairs, or specified affairs, of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.

The Minister may, at any time, with the consent of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, remove an investigator appointed under this Division to investigate the affairs, or specified affairs, of a Local Aboriginal Land Council.

heading.b: Provision of information to Registrar and New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council

block.txt: The Chairperson of an Aboriginal Land Council and any other person who has possession or control of any records of the Council must, if required to do so by the Registrar, provide the Registrar with—
access to such of the records as relate to the operations of the Council requested by the Registrar, and
information that the Chairperson or other person is able to give in relation to those records and operations, and
authorities or orders on bankers and others that relate to those records or operations and that the Chairperson or other person is able to provide.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of an individual—30 penalty units, or
in the case of a corporation—60 penalty units.

The Chairperson of a Local Aboriginal Land Council and any other person who has possession or control of any records of the Council of the Council must, if required to do so by the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, provide the Council with—
access to such of the records as relate to the operations of the Local Aboriginal Land Council requested by the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, and
information that the Chairperson or other person is able to give in relation to those records and operations, and
authorities or orders on bankers and others that relate to those records or operations and that the Chairperson or other person is able to provide.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of an individual—30 penalty units, or
in the case of a corporation—60 penalty units.
If a record—
is not in writing, or
is not written in the English language, or
is not decipherable on sight,

a requirement to provide access to the record is not complied with unless access is provided to a statement, written in the English language and decipherable on sight, that contains all the information in the record.

The Chairperson of an Aboriginal Land Council or any other person who is required to provide the Registrar or the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council with records under section 221A, or provide an investigator with records under section 218, may refuse to comply with the requirements if the record contains privileged communication made by or on behalf of or to an Australian legal practitioner in his or her capacity as an Australian legal practitioner.
The Chairperson or other person may not refuse to comply with a requirement under section 221A to the extent that the person is able to do so without disclosing privileged communication.

If the Chairperson or other person refuses to comply with a requirement because the record is a privileged communication, the Chairperson or other person must, in writing, provide the Registrar with sufficient particulars to identify the record and inform the Registrar that privilege is claimed in relation to the record.
(cf former section 57)

The Minister may at any time appoint, from a list of persons prepared, in accordance with the regulations, by the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, an administrator for a Local Aboriginal Land Council—
if there are not sufficient members of that Council to form a quorum of the Council, or
if the Council fails to furnish satisfactory financial statements and documents to the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council in accordance with Division 2 of Part 8, or
if the Council otherwise fails to comply with section 153 or 158, or

if the Minister is of the opinion, on the receipt of a report by an investigator appointed in accordance with Division 1, or a report by the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, or otherwise, that the funds or other property of the Council have not been properly applied or managed, or
if the Council has substantially breached the requirements of this Act or the regulations or the rules of the Council, or
if the Minister is of the opinion that the Council has ceased for 6 months substantially to exercise its functions, or
if the Council has failed to comply with a compliance direction given under section 235, or

if the Council operates a community benefit schemes for the provision or acquisition of residential accommodation for Aboriginal persons in its area in contravention of a requirement under section 52A that the scheme be approved by the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.

Section 52A(1A) provides that the approval of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council is not required if the Local Aboriginal Land Council is a registered Aboriginal housing organisation (within the meaning of the Aboriginal Housing Act 1998) or a registered community housing provider (within the meaning of the Community Housing Providers National Law (NSW)).
Notice of an appointment of an administrator under this section must be published in the Gazette.
The Minister must not appoint an administrator under this section without the approval of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.
The administrator has, during the period of his or her appointment, to the exclusion of the Council and the Board of the Council—
all, or such part as is specified in the administrator’s instrument of appointment, of the functions of the Board of the Council conferred or imposed by or under this Act, and

the functions of the Council and the members of the Council exercised by resolution of the members of the Council that are prescribed by the regulations (except as provided by the administrator’s instrument of appointment).

The administrator is to be paid out of the funds of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council which may recover the amount paid from the Local Aboriginal Land Council for which the administrator has been appointed.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the functions of the administrator.
Without limiting subsection (6), the regulations may—
specify functions that the administrator must not exercise, except on a resolution of members of the Council, and
specify functions of the Board of the Council that the administrator must not exercise, except on a resolution of members of the Council.

heading.b: Administrators—New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council

block.txt: (cf former section 57A)
The Minister may appoint an administrator of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.
Notice of an appointment of an administrator under this section must be published in the Gazette.

The Minister may appoint an administrator under this section only after considering one of the following reports that discloses, in the opinion of the Minister, grounds that justify the making of such an appointment—
a report of the Auditor-General, or
a report of an investigator appointed in accordance with Division 1.
The Minister must prepare a written report of the Minister’s reasons for appointing an administrator under this section.
The Minister must table a copy of the report in each House of Parliament as soon as practicable after the administrator is appointed.

The administrator has, during the period of his or her appointment, all, or such part as is specified in the administrator’s instrument of appointment, of the functions of the Council conferred or imposed by or under this Act, to the exclusion of the Council.
The administrator is to be paid out of the funds of the Council.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the functions of the administrator.
The Minister may, before appointing an administrator of an Aboriginal Land Council under this Division, give not less than 14 days notice in writing of the appointment to—
in the case of a Local Aboriginal Land Council—each Board member and the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, and
in the case of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council—each councillor.
The Minister must, before appointing an administrator, take into account any written representations received from any person or body to whom notice was given under this section.

heading.b: Interim actions pending appointment of administrator

block.txt: The Minister may, by notice in writing to an Aboriginal Land Council, take any of the following actions, pending the appointment of an administrator of the Council—
prohibit the Council and the Board of the Council from exercising certain specified functions or taking specified actions, except with the approval of the Minister, for a specified period,
appoint a person to act as an interim administrator of the Council for a specified period (not exceeding 3 months).
The interim administrator has, during the period of his or her appointment, to the exclusion of the Council and the Board of the Council—
all, or such part as is specified in the interim administrator’s instrument of appointment, of the functions of the Board of the Council conferred or imposed by or under this Act, and

the functions of the Council and the members of the Council exercised by resolution of the members of the Council that are prescribed by the regulations (except as provided by the interim administrator’s instrument of appointment).
A notice under this section ceases to have effect if an administrator is appointed under this Division or if the Minister decides not to appoint an administrator under this Division.
The Minister must notify the Aboriginal Land Council in writing if the Minister decides not to appoint an administrator.
The Minister may revoke or vary a notice given under this section.
An Aboriginal Land Council must not fail to comply with a notice given under this section.

The interim administrator is to be paid out of the funds of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council and the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may recover that amount from the Local Aboriginal Land Council for which the interim administrator has been appointed.

heading.b: Contents of administrator’s instrument of appointment

block.txt: The instrument by which the Minister appoints an administrator under this Division must specify the following—
whether the administrator is to administer all or only specified functions of the Aboriginal Land Council concerned,
the term of office of the administrator,
the functions and duties of the administrator,
unless remuneration for administrators appointed under this Division is prescribed by the regulations—the remuneration of the administrator,
any other matter prescribed by the regulations.

The instrument may also contain provision for the payment to the administrator of remuneration in addition to the remuneration specified in the instrument. For example, the instrument could provide for the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council to approve the payment of additional remuneration that it is satisfied is reasonable.

heading.b: Certain persons ineligible to be administrators

block.txt: The Minister must not appoint any of the following persons as an administrator of an Aboriginal Land Council—
a councillor,
a Board member,
in the case of the appointment of an administrator of a Local Aboriginal Land Council, a member of that Local Aboriginal Land Council,
a member of staff of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.

heading.b: Removal of office holders on appointment of administrator

block.txt: (cf former section 57B)

On the appointment of an administrator to administer all of the functions of a Local Aboriginal Land Council, the Board members of the Council are removed from office and fresh elections to fill the vacancies are to be held, in the manner specified by the regulations, so as to enable vacancies to be filled at the conclusion of the administrator’s term of office.

On the appointment of an administrator to administer all of the functions of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, the councillors are removed from office and fresh elections to fill the vacancies are to be held, in the manner specified by the regulations, so as to enable vacancies to be filled at the conclusion of the administrator’s term of office.

If an administrator is appointed to administer only specified functions of an Aboriginal Land Council, the officers or councillors (as the case may be) of that Council remain in office and may continue to exercise those functions of the Council not given to the administrator.
(cf clause 94 of 1996 Regulation)

The Chairperson of an Aboriginal Land Council and any other person who has possession or control of any records of the Council must, if required to do so by an administrator who produces evidence of his or her appointment, provide the administrator with—
access to such of the records as relate to the functions of the Council being performed by the administrator, and
information that the Chairperson or other person is able to give in relation to those records and functions, and
authorities or orders on bankers and others that relate to those records or functions and that the Chairperson or other person is able to provide.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of an individual—30 penalty units, or
in the case of a corporation—75 penalty units.
A requirement to provide access to a record that—
is not in writing, or
is not written in the English language, or
is not decipherable on sight,
is not complied with unless access is provided to a statement, written in the English language and decipherable on sight, that contains all the information in the record.
A person must not hinder, obstruct or delay an administrator in the exercise of his or her functions.
Maximum penalty—60 penalty units.

heading.b: Administrator of an Aboriginal Land Council may call meetings

block.txt: The administrator of an Aboriginal Land Council may call meetings of the Council.
The administrator for a Local Aboriginal Land Council must report at least once a month to the following—
the Minister,
the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council,
the Local Aboriginal Land Council concerned.
The administrator of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council must report at least once a month to the following—
the Minister,
the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.
The Minister may give directions to an administrator of an Aboriginal Land Council concerning the form and content of such reports.
The administrator must comply with a direction given under this section.

heading.b: Limitations on certain land dealings by administrator

block.txt: The administrator for a Local Aboriginal Land Council must not dispose of or otherwise deal with land vested in or acquired by the Council without the consent of the Council (as decided at a meeting).
Despite subsection (1), the exercise by an administrator for a Local Aboriginal Land Council of any of the following functions does not require the consent of the Council—
entering into a short-term residential tenancy agreement,
the management of a short-term residential tenancy agreement,
the termination of a short-term residential tenancy agreement,

if the administrator was appointed on one or more grounds, including that the Local Aboriginal Land Council had operated a community benefits scheme for the provision or acquisition of residential accommodation for Aboriginal persons in its area in contravention of a requirement under section 52A that the scheme be approved by the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council—a dealing that is necessary for the purposes of—
obtaining the approval of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council to the operation of the scheme, or
operating the scheme as a registered Aboriginal housing organisation (within the meaning of the Aboriginal Housing Act 1998), or
operating the scheme as a registered community housing provider (within the meaning of the Community Housing Providers National Law (NSW)).

heading.b: Minister may amend instrument of appointment of administrator

block.txt: The Minister may extend the term of office of an administrator of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.
The Minister may, with the consent of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, extend the term of office of an administrator for a Local Aboriginal Land Council.
The Minister may, by subsequent instrument of appointment, vary the functions that may be exercised by an administrator during the extension of the administrator’s term of appointment.
The Minister may, at any time, remove an administrator of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.
The Minister may, at any time, with the consent of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, remove an administrator for a Local Aboriginal Land Council.

heading.b: Non-functioning Aboriginal Land Councils and assistance to Local Aboriginal Land Councils
Failure of NSW Aboriginal Land Council to function

block.txt: (cf former section 58)

If, in the opinion of the Minister, the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council has wilfully failed or neglected to exercise any of its functions in a material respect, the Governor may, by order published in the Gazette, declare that the Council has ceased to function.
An order under subsection (1) may be limited in its operation according to time, place or circumstance.

If the Governor has made an order under subsection (1), the Minister may make, in writing, orders relating to the transfer, disposal or dealing with the assets, debts and liabilities of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council as the Minister considers appropriate (having regard to the objects of that Council set out in section 105) and those orders have effect according to their tenor.

heading.b: Performance improvement orders for Local Aboriginal Land Councils

block.txt: The New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may make a performance improvement order in respect of a Local Aboriginal Land Council if the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council reasonably considers that action must be taken to improve the performance of the Local Aboriginal Land Council.
In determining whether to make a performance improvement order, the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council—
must consider the performance improvement criteria prescribed by the regulations (if any), and

may consider any previous communication between the Local Aboriginal Land Council concerned and the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council in relation to the Local Aboriginal Land Council’s performance.

Without limiting subsection (2), the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may consider any other matter that the Council considers to be appropriate when determining whether to make a performance improvement order.
A performance improvement order must specify—
the reason for making the order, and
the actions that are required to be taken to improve the performance of the Local Aboriginal Land Council.

Actions to improve the performance of a Local Aboriginal Land Council may include any actions that the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council considers necessary to improve or restore the proper or effective functioning of the Local Aboriginal Land Council.
The performance improvement order may require action to be taken by any or all of the following—
the Local Aboriginal Land Council,
the Board or individual Board members of the Local Aboriginal Land Council,
the chief executive officer of the Local Aboriginal Land Council.
A performance improvement order may provide for the appointment of an advisor in accordance with this Division.
A copy of the performance improvement order, or the variation of a performance improvement order, is to be served on the Local Aboriginal Land Council.
A performance improvement order takes effect on the day on which it is served on the Local Aboriginal Land Council concerned, or such later date as may be specified in the order.

The making of a performance improvement order, or the fact that any such order is in force, does not derogate from any power of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council or any other person to make any order or take any other action under this Act.

A performance improvement order in respect of a Local Aboriginal Land Council ceases to be in force if the Minister appoints an administrator or interim administrator for the Local Aboriginal Land Council.
In relation to a performance improvement order, a reference to an action, or the taking of any action, includes a reference to doing any thing or refraining from doing any thing.

A Local Aboriginal Land Council must provide a copy of a performance improvement order to the members of the Council at the first meeting of the Council held after the performance improvement order is made in respect of the Council.
The Board of a Local Aboriginal Land Council is responsible for ensuring the Council’s compliance with a performance improvement order.

A Local Aboriginal Land Council complies with a performance improvement order only if any action required to be taken by the performance improvement order (including any actions required to be taken by individual Board members or the chief executive officer) is taken to the satisfaction of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.

A Local Aboriginal Land Council must provide the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council with written reports on its compliance with a performance improvement order as required by the order (a compliance report).
A compliance report must specify any actions taken that demonstrate compliance with the performance improvement order.
A compliance report must comply with any requirements for the report specified in the performance improvement order.

A Local Aboriginal Land Council must provide a copy of a compliance report to the members of the Council at the first meeting of the Council held after the report is provided to the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.

If the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council makes a performance improvement order in respect of a Local Aboriginal Land Council, the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may appoint one or more persons as advisors to the Local Aboriginal Land Council.
An advisor may be appointed at the same time as the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council makes the performance improvement order or at any time while the order remains in force.
An advisor may be appointed on the recommendation of the Local Aboriginal Land Council or on the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council’s own initiative.
An advisor has, subject to any limitations specified in the advisor’s instrument of appointment, the following functions—
to advise and assist the Board of the Local Aboriginal Land Council and the Council in the exercise of their functions,
to advise and assist the Board of the Local Aboriginal Land Council and the Council in complying with the performance improvement order,
to monitor compliance with the performance improvement order.
An advisor’s appointment to a Local Aboriginal Land Council ends on the earlier of the following—
the end of the term specified in the advisor’s instrument of appointment,
the day on which the performance improvement order for the Local Aboriginal Land Council expires, is revoked or otherwise ceases to be in force.
The New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may terminate an advisor’s appointment at any time.

The advisor is to be paid a salary determined by the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council out of the funds of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council and the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may recover that amount from the Local Aboriginal Land Council for which the advisor has been appointed.

If an advisor is appointed to a Local Aboriginal Land Council, the Council and its Board members and staff are required to co-operate with the advisor and provide any information or assistance the advisor reasonably requires to exercise his or her functions.

In particular, the Local Aboriginal Land Council must give the advisor an opportunity to review a compliance report at least 14 days before providing the report to the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council and must include a copy of the advisor’s comments (if any) when providing the compliance report to the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.
If a Local Aboriginal Land Council fails to give an advisor an opportunity to comment on a compliance report, the advisor is to—
inform the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council of that fact, and
give the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council a report on the Local Aboriginal Land Council’s compliance with the performance improvement order.

If a Local Aboriginal Land Council fails to provide a compliance report to the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council in accordance with a performance improvement order, the advisor must, as soon as practicable after becoming aware of that fact—
prepare a compliance report on behalf of the Local Aboriginal Land Council, and
provide the report to the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council.
A contravention of this section by a Local Aboriginal Land Council is, for the purposes of this Division, a failure to comply with a performance improvement order.

Any person or body may request the Registrar to issue a direction to an Aboriginal Land Council or an officer of an Aboriginal Land Council requiring the Council or officer to comply with a specified provision or provisions of this Act or of any regulations or rules made under this Act.

If the Registrar is satisfied that an Aboriginal Land Council or an officer of an Aboriginal Land Council has failed to comply, or is not complying, with a specified provision or provisions of this Act or of any regulations or rules made under this Act, the Registrar may issue a direction to the Council or officer requiring the Council or officer to comply with that provision or those provisions within a time stated in the direction.
The Registrar is not to issue a direction under this Part in relation to any matter if—
the matter could constitute an offence under this Act or any other law, or
provision is made for the determination of the matter under another section of this Act.
In this section—
officer, in relation to an Aboriginal Land Council, includes—
for a Local Aboriginal Land Council—the chief executive officer of the Council, and
for the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council—the Chief Executive Officer of the Council.

heading.b: Registrar may refer failure to comply to Court

block.txt: If an Aboriginal Land Council or an officer of an Aboriginal Land Council does not comply with a direction issued under this Part within the time stated in the direction, the Registrar may refer the matter that is the subject of the direction to the Court for determination.
The Court must hear and determine any matter referred to it by the Registrar under this Part.
The Court may give such directions as it considers necessary to determine a matter referred to it.
Any person who contravenes a direction given by the Court under this Part is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of an individual—80 penalty units, or
in the case of a corporation—200 penalty units.
This Part applies to a dispute concerning the operation of this Act or the regulations.
This Part does not apply to a dispute if—
the dispute relates to a matter that could constitute an offence under this Act or the regulations or any other law, or
provision is made for the resolution or determination of the dispute under another provision of this Act (other than under Part 12) or the regulations.

heading.b: Mediation, conciliation or arbitration of disputes by NSW Aboriginal Land Council

block.txt: The New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may, if the parties to a dispute to which this Part applies (other than a dispute to which that Council is a party) have agreed, attempt to resolve the dispute by mediation, conciliation or arbitration.

The New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may, if the parties to the dispute have agreed, refer a dispute to which this Part applies (other than a dispute to which the Council is a party) to mediation, conciliation or arbitration by the Registrar or another independent person.
The Registrar may, if the parties to a dispute to which this Part applies have agreed—
attempt to resolve the dispute by mediation, conciliation or arbitration, or
refer the dispute to mediation, conciliation or arbitration by an independent person.

heading.b: Compulsory mediation of land dealing application disputes

block.txt: This section applies to a dispute relating to a decision by the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council under Division 4 of Part 2 to approve or not to approve a land dealing.
A Local Aboriginal Land Council must, if the Council proposes to commence legal proceedings in relation to the dispute, refer the dispute to the Registrar.
The Registrar may, with the parties consent—
attempt to resolve the dispute by mediation, conciliation or arbitration, or
refer the dispute to mediation, conciliation or arbitration by an independent person.

Subject to this Act and the regulations, the Commercial Arbitration Act 2010 applies to an arbitration undertaken by the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council, the Registrar or an independent person under this Part.

The provisions of the Commercial Arbitration Act 2010 apply to an arbitration under this Act with the modification that a reference in that Act to the Court or the Supreme Court is to be taken to be a reference to the Land and Environment Court.

The Commercial Arbitration Act 2010 contains machinery and other provisions applying to arbitrations. The provisions applying to arbitrations under that Act set out the way in which arbitrators are to conduct arbitration proceedings and powers to require evidence to be given, as well as parties’ rights to representation and other procedural matters. They also provide that an award by an arbitrator is to be final unless set aside under that Act and provide for enforcement procedures. An appeal to a Court on a question of law is also available under that Act.
(cf former section 59)
The Registrar may refer a dispute to which this Part applies to the Court for determination.
The Court must hear and determine any dispute referred to it by the Registrar under this section.
The Court may give such directions as it considers necessary to determine a dispute referred to it.
Any person who contravenes a direction given by the Court under this section is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of an individual—80 penalty units, or
in the case of a corporation—200 penalty units.
(cf former section 54)
An act or omission of an Aboriginal Land Council, or any of the following persons—
a councillor,
a member of any Local Aboriginal Land Council or Board member or chief executive officer of a Local Aboriginal Land Council,
a member of an advisory committee,
an advisor to a Local Aboriginal Land Council,
the Chief Executive Officer of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council,
a member of staff of an Aboriginal Land Council,
any person acting under the direction of an Aboriginal Land Council,
a person who is a member of an expert advisory panel constituted under section 42I,

does not subject a councillor, member, advisor, Chief Executive Officer, member of staff or person so acting personally to any action, liability, claim or demand if the act or omission was done, or omitted to be done, in good faith for the purpose of executing this or any other Act.
An act or omission of any of the following persons—
the Registrar,
an investigator,
an administrator,
a person acting as a mediator, conciliator or arbitrator under Part 13,

does not subject the Registrar, investigator, administrator or person so acting personally to any action, liability, claim or demand if the act or omission was done, or omitted to be done, in good faith for the purpose of executing this or any other Act.
(cf former section 55(1))
The Minister may delegate to any person any of the functions of the Minister under this Act, other than this power of delegation.

heading.b: Effect of suspension of Board members and councillors

block.txt: A councillor or Board member, while suspended from office under this Act—
is not entitled to exercise any functions of the office, and
is not entitled to any fee or other remuneration to which he or she would otherwise be entitled as the holder of the office, and
is not to be counted as a voting member of the Council or Board for the purposes of determining the quorum required for a meeting of the Council or Board.
(cf former section 62)
A document may be served on an Aboriginal Land Council by leaving it at, or by sending it by post to—
the office of the Council, or
if it has more than one office—any one of its offices,
or, where some other manner of service is prescribed by the regulations, by serving it in the manner prescribed.

Nothing in subsection (1) affects the operation of any provision of a law or of the rules of a court authorising a document to be served on an Aboriginal Land Council in a manner not provided for by subsection (1).
The New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council may execute a document without using a common seal if the document is signed by—
the Chairperson of the Council, or
a councillor or member of staff of the Council authorised by the Chairperson.
A Local Aboriginal Land Council may execute a document without using a common seal if the document is signed by—
the Chairperson of the Board of the Local Aboriginal Land Council, or
a Board member or member of staff of the Local Aboriginal Land Council authorised by the Chairperson.

heading.b: Proof of certain matters not required

block.txt: (cf former section 64)
In any legal proceedings, no proof is required (until evidence is given to the contrary) of—
the constitution of an Aboriginal Land Council, or
any resolution of an Aboriginal Land Council, or
the appointment or election of any councillor or any Board member, or
the holding of office by a person as an officer of the New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council or as the Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson of a Board, or
the presence or nature of a quorum at any meeting of an Aboriginal Land Council.
This section applies to a resolution of an Aboriginal Land Council or a certificate issued under this Act by an Aboriginal Land Council.

The Chairperson of an Aboriginal Land Council may, on the application of a person or on the Chairperson’s own initiative, correct any of the following in any document to which this section applies that was created or issued by that Council—
a clerical mistake,
an error arising from an accidental slip or omission,
a mistake in the description of any person or thing,
a defect of form.

heading.b: Aboriginal Land Councils not statutory bodies representing the Crown

block.txt: (cf former section 65)
An Aboriginal Land Council is not, for the purposes of any law, a statutory body representing the Crown.

heading.b: Aboriginal Land Councils to be public authorities etc for certain purposes

block.txt: (cf former section 65A)

Each Aboriginal Land Council is taken to be a public authority for the purposes of the Ombudsman Act 1974, the Independent Commission Against Corruption Act 1988 and the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009.
Despite subsection (1), a Local Aboriginal Land Council is not taken to be an agency for the purposes of section 6 of the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009.
The Registrar may apply to an authorised officer for a search warrant if the Registrar has reasonable grounds for believing—
that a provision of this Act or the regulations has been or is being contravened, or
that records required to be provided to an investigator under section 218 have not been so provided, or
that records required to be provided to an administrator under section 227 have not been so provided.

An authorised officer to whom an application for a search warrant is made under this section may, if satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for doing so, issue a search warrant authorising the Registrar, when accompanied by a police officer, and any other person named in the warrant—
to enter specified premises, and
to search the premises for evidence of a contravention of this Act or the regulations or records required to be provided to an investigator or administrator, that have not been so provided.
Division 4 of Part 5 of the Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002 applies to a search warrant issued under this section.
In this section—
authorised officer means an authorised officer within the meaning of the Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002.
If the Court is satisfied on the application of the Registrar that a person has engaged or is proposing to engage in conduct that constitutes or would constitute—
a contravention of a provision of this Act or the regulations, or
an attempt to contravene such a provision, or
aiding, abetting, counselling or procuring a person to contravene such a provision, or
inducing, or attempting to induce, whether by threats or promises or otherwise, a person to contravene such a provision, or
being in any way, directly or indirectly, knowingly concerned in, or party to, the contravention by a person of such a provision, or
conspiring with others to contravene such a provision,
the Court may grant an injunction in such terms as the Court determines to be appropriate.
If in the opinion of the Court it is desirable to do so, the Court may grant an interim injunction pending determination of the application.
The Court may rescind or vary an injunction granted under this section.

When the Registrar makes an application to the Court for the grant of an injunction under this section, the Court is not to require the Registrar or any other person, as a condition of granting an interim injunction, to give any undertakings as to damages.
(cf former section 67)
Proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations are to be dealt with summarily.

If a corporation contravenes, whether by act or omission, any provision of this Act or the regulations, each person who is a director of the corporation or who is concerned in the management of the corporation is taken to have contravened the same provision if the person knowingly authorised or permitted the contravention.
A person may be proceeded against and convicted under a provision pursuant to subsection (1) whether or not the corporation has been proceeded against or has been convicted under the provision.
Nothing in this section affects any liability imposed on a corporation for an offence committed by the corporation under this Act or the regulations.

heading.b: Establishment of new Local Aboriginal Land Councils

block.txt: If, after the commencement of Schedule 1 [17] to the Aboriginal Land Rights Amendment Act 2001, a Local Aboriginal Land Council is constituted by this Act—
the Registrar (or a person appointed by the Registrar) is to prepare a membership roll for the Council under section 54(1), and
the first meeting of the Council is to be held at a time (being a time as soon as practicable after its constitution) and place determined by the Registrar, and
until a Chairperson of the Board is elected at that first meeting, the Registrar (or a person appointed by the Registrar) is to preside at that meeting, and
at the first meeting of the Council, the members are to elect the Board of the Council.
Despite section 54, when first prepared as required by subsection (1), the membership roll is to contain the names and addresses of those adult Aboriginal persons—
who—
reside in the Local Aboriginal Council area concerned, or
have a sufficient association with that area or are Aboriginal owners of land in that area, and
who have requested in writing that they be enrolled as members of the Council, and
who have been accepted by the Registrar (or a person appointed by the Registrar under subsection (1)(a)) as members.
(cf former section 68)

The Governor may make regulations, not inconsistent with this Act, for or with respect to any matter that by this Act is required or permitted to be prescribed or that is necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
Without affecting the generality of subsection (1), the Governor may make regulations for or with respect to the following—
determining the boundaries of, and naming, Local Aboriginal Land Council areas,
the keeping of minutes of meetings of Aboriginal Land Councils and the access to those minutes by other Aboriginal Land Councils and other persons and bodies,
the investment of money by Aboriginal Land Councils, including regulations for or with respect to the prescribing or the determining of the proportion of the funds of those Councils to be invested,
the audit of accounts and records of Aboriginal Land Councils (including regulations for or with respect to the employment of auditors),
disputed returns in elections of councillors,
the fees, allowances or expenses that may be paid to investigators and administrators of Aboriginal Land Councils,
the preparation and maintenance of membership rolls of Local Aboriginal Land Councils, and the time and manner in which those rolls must be provided to the Registrar,
the keeping and operation of the Register of Aboriginal Land Claims and the Register of Aboriginal Owners,
the making of Aboriginal Land Agreements under section 36AA.

A regulation made for the purposes of subsection (2)(a) may apply to the matters referred to in that paragraph any provisions (with any necessary alterations) of this Act relating to the constitution of Local Aboriginal Land Council areas.
A regulation may create an offence punishable by a penalty not exceeding 10 penalty units.
The Minister is to review this Act to determine whether the policy objectives of the Act remain valid and whether the terms of the Act remain appropriate for securing those objectives.

The review is to be undertaken as soon as possible after the period of 5 years from the date of assent to the Aboriginal Land Rights Amendment Act 2006 and as soon as possible after the end of every period of 5 years thereafter.
A report on the outcome of a review is to be tabled in each House of Parliament within 12 months after the end of the period of 5 years.
